message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (²H, 0.02 %) – stable; Tritium (³H) – radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y) |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | 0.754 eV (73 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 g cm⁻³) |
| **State at room temperature** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas |
| **Molecular form** | Diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions |
| **Bond type** | Covalent (single σ bond) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), reacts with halogens (HX), oxidizes to water (combustion) |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂) |
| **Solubility in water** | Low (~0.0006 g g⁻¹ at 25 °C) |
| **Role in biology** | Essential component of water, organic molecules, fuels (e.g., glucose oxidation) |
| **Role in astrophysics** | Most abundant element in the universe; primary fuel for stellar fusion (proton–proton chain, CNO cycle) |
| **Physical characteristics** | Lowest density of all gases; lowest boiling/melting points; high specific heat capacity (gas) |
| **Chemical behavior** | Forms +1 cations (H⁺) in acids; forms –1 anions (H⁻) in hydrides; participates in hydrogen bonding as a donor (in H₂O, NH₃, etc.) |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), rocket propellant, laboratory reagent |

---

### Quick Summary

- **Elemental identity:** Hydrogen is the lightest and simplest element (one proton, one electron).
- **Physical state:** Gas at ambient conditions; extremely low density and boiling/melting points.
- **Chemical nature:** Nonmetal, diatomic (H₂), highly reactive, forms both covalent bonds and ionic species (H⁺, H⁻).
- **Isotopic diversity:** Stable protium and deuterium; radioactive tritium.
- **Universal abundance:** Most common element in the cosmos; key player in stellar nucleosynthesis.
- **Practical uses:** Energy carrier (fuel cells, rockets), industrial chemistry (hydrogenation, ammonia production), laboratory reagent.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property!
